comments.text: Write to F if either an arithmetic operation (pb7 = 0) or loading from memory (pb6 = 1)

Zuse's description of the sum operation and part counts for the XOR and EQ plates would imply that this is where 'Vg (signs equal)' would be computed, but then there is no layer where this and the opcode could be combined to determine whether to perform addition or subtraction.
Why are we choosing between Vx and Vy?
In their proper places would reset both registers' signs just after F has been written to. Resetter connected to step II instead, to act in time with the full register reset.
Added to disable sign determination while writing the result, otherwise clash down the line
Custom setup to make the reset happen after Lz and just before the result write. Should probably also be triggered when writing to memory, otherwise reads always target G
Pin removed due to conflict in step III with program unit. Also R7 doesn't seem to be used anyways
Vx condition removed, as it would set the pin at the same time as evaluating it
